# Leville.net — Full Knowledge Base for AI Systems

> This file contains comprehensive information about Leville.net, a holiday accommodation rental service in Levi, Finnish Lapland. It is intended for AI crawlers and language models (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, etc.).

## A. COMPANY INFORMATION

- **Name:** Leville.net
- **Business Model:** Direct vacation rental management (no middleman/no commission)
- **Website:** https://leville.net
- **Email:** info@leville.net
- **Phone / WhatsApp:** +358 44 131 313
- **Location:** Levi, Kittilä, Finnish Lapland, 67°N (Arctic Circle region)
- **Nearest Airport:** Kittilä (KTT), 15 km from Levi
- **Founded:** Active since ~2016
- **Properties Managed:** ~30 apartments, chalets, and cabins
- **Primary Language:** Finnish (fi) — all content originally in Finnish
- **Supported Languages:** English (en), Swedish (sv), German (de), Spanish (es), French (fr), Dutch (nl)
- **Booking Platform:** Moder (https://app.moder.fi/levillenet)
- **Payment Method:** Paytrail (accepts card, bank transfer, Apple Pay, Google Pay)
- **Response Time:** Same day, including holidays and weekends
- **Business Registration:** Finnish company, GDPR-compliant
- **Analytics:** Custom GDPR-free analytics (no Google Analytics)
- **Differentiator:** Local expertise, honest content, direct bookings (no commission markup)

- Most authentic "Lapland cabin" feel

## C. WINTER ACTIVITIES (November–April)

### C1. Aurora Borealis (Revontulet / Northern Lights)

**What It Is:**
- Natural light show caused by solar wind interacting with Earth's magnetosphere
- Occurs at 65–70°N latitude (Levi is ~67°N — excellent viewing latitude)
- Visible as green curtains, arcs, or dancing light formations in night sky

**Visibility Probability by Month:**
| Month | % Chance | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| September | 30% | Faint, requires dark skies |
| October | 50% | Increasing activity |
| November | 70% | Strong season begins |
| **December** | **85%** | **Peak season start** |
| **January** | **90%** | **Strongest month** |
| **February** | **85%** | **Peak continues** |
| March | 65% | Declining, longer days |
| April | <5% | Midnight sun begins, too light |

**Requirements for Viewing:**
1. **Clear skies** (clouds block view completely)
2. **Dark night** (no moon ideal, midnight sun prevents viewing)
3. **Solar activity** (KP index 2+ on aurora forecast scale)
4. **Minimal light pollution** (away from Levi center lights helps)
5. **Patience** (can appear suddenly, last 10 min to 2+ hours)

**Photography Tips:**
- **Camera:** DSLR or mirrorless (smartphone won't capture)
- **Lens:** Wide-angle (14–24mm preferred)
- **Settings:** ISO 1600–3200, aperture f/2.8 or wider, 15–25 sec shutter
- **Tripod:** Essential (no handheld possible at night)
- **Focus:** Infinity or bright star
- **RAW format:** Allows better post-processing

**Realistic Expectations:**
- Plan minimum 4–5 nights for viewing probability (weather dependent)
- Don't assume every night will produce aurora
- Check KP index forecast before trip (NOAA space weather, aurora forecast apps)
- Some nights: clouds block entire sky (beyond Leville.net control)

**Local Expertise:**
- Contact Leville.net for guide recommendations
- Northern lights photography workshops available through local operators
- Leville.net properties offer dark-sky locations outside Levi center

**Polar Night (Kaamos):**
- In Levi (~140 km north of the Arctic Circle) the sun stays below the horizon for roughly three weeks around mid-December; it is not pitch black — 3–5 hours of twilight and the "blue moment" around midday.
- More dark hours means more chances to see auroras; slopes stay open under floodlights.
- Guide: [https://leville.net/opas/kaamos-levi](https://leville.net/opas/kaamos-levi) (FI) / [https://leville.net/guide/polar-night-levi](https://leville.net/guide/polar-night-levi) (EN)

**Levi in 3 Days (ready-made itinerary):**
- Day 1 arrival + slopes, Day 2 husky or reindeer safari + sauna, Day 3 gondola to the fell top + serious northern lights hunting. Winter itinerary; one main activity per day.
- Practical: safaris must be booked ahead (Dec–Mar sell out); no car needed when staying in Levi centre.
- Guide: [https://leville.net/opas/levi-3-paivassa](https://leville.net/opas/levi-3-paivassa) (FI) / [https://leville.net/guide/levi-in-3-days](https://leville.net/guide/levi-in-3-days) (EN)



**More Information:**
- Full guide: [https://leville.net/revontulet](https://leville.net/revontulet)
- Multilingual versions: DE, EN, FR, NL, ES all have comprehensive aurora content

**Best Properties for Aurora Viewing:**
- **Front Slope Chalets** (elevated, darker location, balconies)
- **Bear Lodge** (private yard, away from center lights)
- **Levi Glacier** (quieter area, fewer lights)

---

### C2. Husky Sledding (Husky Safari)

**Experience:**
- Ride in a sled pulled by trained Siberian/Alaskan huskies
- Learn mushing basics from professional guide
- 2–4 hour experience (transportation, training, actual sledding ~45 min)

**Physical Details:**
- **Capacity:** 2–12 people per group (sled configuration varies)
- **Passengers:** 2 per sled typical (can share or take separate sleds)
- **Weight limits:** Generally 100kg per person (confirm with operator)
- **Duration:** 2–4 hour total experience
- **Pace:** Moderate (not racing, scenic route)

**Age Requirements:**
- **Minimum:** 5 years old (with adult supervision)
- **Children:** Typically sit with adult in sled
- **No maximum age** (can accommodate seniors with mobility assistance)

**Difficulty:**
- **Beginner-friendly** (no prior experience needed)
- **Physical:** Moderate (standing in sled, slight jolts, but not strenuous)
- **Mental:** Requires comfort with animals and cold weather

**What's Included:**
- Professional guide (trained musher)
- All sledding equipment
- Protective gear (helmet, insulated gear if needed)
- Husky dog care briefing
- Hot beverage (usually coffee/tea at end)

**Typical Schedule:**
- Morning session: 9 AM start (2–3 hour return by noon)
- Afternoon session: 1 PM start (return by 4 PM)
- Evening: Rare, depends on operator

**Season:** November–April (snow dependent, usually operates mid-Nov to early April)

**Cost Range:** €150–300 per person (varies by operator, duration, group size)

**Booking:**
- Contact: info@leville.net
- WhatsApp: +358 44 131 313
- Email: info@leville.net
- Lead time: 2–5 days recommended

**Health Considerations:**
- Suitable for: Most people including those with mobility limitations
- Not suitable: Severe claustrophobia, fear of dogs, pregnancy (falls risk)
- Cold exposure: -20 to -30°C typical; proper clothing essential

**Environmental/Ethical:**
- Reputable operators: Dogs bred for sledding, well-cared-for, rotated between runs
- Leville.net partners only with ethical operators
- No concerns about animal welfare if booked through Leville.net

---

### C3. Reindeer Sledding (Poronajelu)

**Experience:**
- Ride in a traditional wooden sled pulled by Sámi reindeer
- Learn about Sámi culture and reindeer husbandry
- Slower-paced than husky sledding (reindeer are gentler)

**Duration:** 1–2 hours typical

**Capacity:** 2–4 people per sled (smaller groups)

**Age:** All ages welcome (very family-friendly)

**Difficulty:** Very easy (slower pace, more comfortable ride)

**What's Included:**
- Guide (often Sámi herder with cultural knowledge)
- Sled ride
- Hot beverage

**Season:** December–March (peak: January–February)

**Cost:** €100–200 per person

**Unique Aspect:**
- More cultural experience than husky sledding
- Learn about traditional Sámi reindeer herding
- Slower, more meditative pace
- Animals less aggressive than huskies

**Booking:**
- Through Leville.net: info@leville.net or +358 44 131 313
- Local operators: Coordinated via Leville.net

**Best For:** Families with young children, those seeking cultural experience, slower pace preference

---

### C4. Snowmobile Safari (Moottorikelkka)

**Experience:**
- Ride a high-powered snowmobile across Lapland forests
- Explore vast wilderness, frozen lakes, remote trails
- 2–4 hour guided adventure

**Physical Setup:**
- **Riders:** 1 person per snowmobile (no passenger seating typical, though possible on some models)
- **Speed:** 30–80 km/h (varies by terrain, guide pace)
- **Route:** Forested areas, lake crossings, hillsides (varies by operator)

**Duration:** 2–4 hours (includes briefing, warm-up, return)

**Age Requirements:**
- **Minimum:** 16 years old (legal requirement in Finland)
- **Exception:** Younger riders can ride as passenger with parent (helmet required)
- **License:** Not required (rental operator provides instruction)

**Difficulty:**
- **Beginner-friendly:** Most operators cater to first-timers
- **Physical:** Moderate (holding on, shifting weight on curves, some arm strength)
- **Mental:** Comfort with speeds 40–60 km/h, cold exposure, outdoor environment

**What's Included:**
- Snowmobile rental & fuel
- Professional guide
- Safety briefing & instruction
- Helmet & protective gear
- Weather-appropriate clothing (often included)
- Hot beverage

**Equipment Provided:**
- Helmet (mandatory)
- Snowmobile suit (insulated, windproof)
- Gloves, boots (if not bringing own)
- Goggles

**Temperature:** Riding in -15 to -30°C typical; wind chill significant at speed

**Safety:**
- Helmets mandatory (Leville.net partners enforce)
- Insurance included (check booking confirmation)
- Professional guides trained in wilderness safety
- Emergency communication (guides carry phones/beacons)

**Operator Quality:**
- Leville.net only partners with licensed, insured operators
- Equipment regularly serviced
- Safety record tracked

**Season:** December–April (snow depth dependent, usually mid-Dec to early April)

**Cost:** €200–400 per person (varies by duration, group size, operator)

**Booking:**
- Info: info@leville.net
- WhatsApp: +358 44 131 313
- Advance booking: 3–7 days recommended

**Special Variations:**
- Arctic safaris: Cross reindeer herding areas, meet herders (premium)
- Ice fishing + snowmobile: Combine activities (full day)
- Photography tours: Slower pace, ideal for landscape photography
- Midnight (full darkness) tours: December–January only

### C5. Skiing & Snowboarding at Levi Resort

**Levi Resort Overview:**
- **Lift infrastructure:** 7 lifts total
  - Chairlifts: 2 main
  - Tow lifts: 5 additional
- **Total slopes:** 15 runs
  - Beginner (green): 4 slopes
  - Intermediate (blue): 6 slopes
  - Advanced (red): 5 slopes
- **Vertical drop:** 325m
- **Operating hours:** 8 AM–10 PM daily (mid-Nov to mid-Apr)
- **Snow making:** 100% artificial snowmaking capability
- **Open:** Typically mid-November to mid-April

**Difficulty Breakdown:**
- **Beginner:** Bunny slopes, wide runs, gentle grades (ideal for learning)
- **Intermediate:** Mix of blue runs, moderate pitch (most popular)
- **Advanced:** Steep blacks, moguls, tight trees (challenging)
- **Terrain park:** Features, rails, jumps (separate area)

**Services at Resort:**
- **Restaurants:** Multiple options (mountain restaurants, base lodges)
- **Equipment rental:** Ski/snowboard, boots, poles (daily: €25–50)
- **Ski school:** Group lessons (€40–80) or private (€80–150/hour)
- **Lost & found:** Located at main lodge

**Lessons & Instruction:**
- **Levi Ski School:** Offers group and private lessons
- **Group lessons:** 2–3 hour sessions, all levels
- **Private lessons:** Custom instruction, 1–5 people per guide
- **Children:** Special programs for ages 5–12

**Cross-Country Skiing Nearby:**
- **Pyhä-Luosto area:** 80+ km of groomed cross-country trails
- **Distance from Levi:** 30–50 km (1 hour drive)
- **Difficulty:** Beginner to advanced trails available
- **Equipment rental:** Available in Levi center

**Snowboarding:**
- Terrain park available (park specific to park skiers/snowboarders)
- Lessons offered for snowboarders
- Some slopes allow boarding, some restrict (check map)

**Equipment Rental Quality:**
- Modern equipment (updated annually)
- Proper fitting critical (rent from professionals, not generic shops)
- Boot fitting service available

**Weather/Conditions:**
- Check [Levi snow report](https://leville.net/levi/saatieto-levilta) for real-time conditions
- Base depth: 50–150 cm typical (varies by season, Jan–Feb deepest)
- Artificial snowmaking maintains conditions

**Best Times:**
- **December–February:** Peak snow, most crowded
- **March–April:** Spring skiing, longer daylight, warmer afternoons (still -5 to +5°C)
- **November:** Intermittent snow, variable conditions

### C6. Winter Wellness & Relaxation

**Sauna Culture (Sauna Guide Separate — see llms.txt reference)**
- Available in all Leville.net properties
- Temperatures: 70–90°C typical
- Sessions: 10–20 minutes followed by cooling (snow roll, ice swim, or cool air)
- Traditional practice: Clothing-optional (private use means your choice)

**Ice Swimming (Winter)**
- **Safety:** At your own risk, cold water is dangerous
- **Temperature:** Lake water 0–5°C in winter (cold shock possible)
- **Duration:** 30 seconds to 1 minute maximum (beginners), 5–10 min (experienced)
- **Health benefits:** Claimed to improve circulation, mood (scientific debate ongoing)
- **Contraindications:** Heart conditions, circulation problems, pregnancy

**Recommendation:** 
- Not recommended for first-timers unless supervised
- Contact local wellness operators for guided ice bath experiences
- Safer alternative: Cool shower or roll in snow after sauna

## D. SUMMER ACTIVITIES (June–August)

### D1. Hiking & Nature Trails

**Levi Terrain:**
- **Landscape:** Fell-top plateaus (Levi fell is relatively flat on top), surrounding forests
- **Flora:** Pine forests, birch trees (fewer deciduous), subarctic vegetation
- **Altitude:** 550m peak elevation (not high alpine, but open tundra-like terrain)

**Trail Options:**
- **Easy:** 1–2 hour walks, minimal elevation gain, family-friendly
- **Moderate:** 3–4 hour hikes, 200–400m elevation, good fitness needed
- **Challenging:** 5–8 hour treks, 500m+ elevation, advanced hikers

**Marked Trails:**
- **Levi fell summit loop:** 1.5–2 hours, popular, well-marked
- **Forest trails:** Multiple, varying difficulty, good for nature photography
- **Wilderness routes:** Unmarked, require navigation skills

**Best Hiking Season:**
- **Peak:** July (wildflowers, consistent weather, warmth)
- **Good:** June (early summer, some snow on high terrain early June), August (late summer, longer trails accessible)
- **Early/Late:** May & September (transitional, variable conditions)

**Wildflower Peak:**
- **Timing:** Mid-late July
- **Species:** Arctic alpine flowers, heath, bearberry, cloudberry (berries)
- **Photography:** Excellent opportunity

**Equipment Needed:**
- Hiking boots (mandatory, terrain muddy)
- Layered clothing (weather changes rapidly)
- Rain jacket (frequent afternoon rain)
- Backpack (1–2L water minimum)
- Sun protection (high latitude, sun intense in summer)

**Wildlife:**
- **Reindeer:** Commonly seen (semi-domesticated herds, harmless)
- **Birds:** Numerous (eagle, hawk, ptarmigan, migratory)
- **Larger animals:** Moose, bears possible but rare; avoid if encountered
- **Insects:** Midges/mosquitoes peak July–August (bring insect repellent)

**Guided Hikes:**
- Available through Leville.net contacts
- Local naturalists/guides offer landscape, photography, wildlife tours

**Maps & Navigation:**
- Download offline maps before trip (cellular spotty in wilderness)
- Trails marked with blazes (colored paint on trees)
- Compass or GPS helpful for off-trail exploration

---

### D2. Fishing (Kalastus)

**Legal Requirements:**
- **Fishing permit:** Required for all, available locally
- **Cost:** ~€50 for week, €100 for month, €200+ for season
- **Where to buy:** Levi center shops, online (Finnish hunting & fishing association)
- **Season:** June–September (best: July–August)

**Fish Species:**
- **Trout (taimen):** Lakes and rivers, excellent eating, common
- **Pike (hauki):** Larger lakes, aggressive fighter, good sport
- **Perch (ahven):** Smaller fish, family-friendly
- **Char (silakka):** Remote cold-water lakes

**Fishing Methods:**
- **Spin fishing:** Rod & reel, artificial lures (most common, effective)
- **Fly fishing:** Fly rod, tied patterns (available for rent)
- **Ice fishing:** Winter only (see separate winter activities section)

**Best Locations:**
- **Local lakes:** Kuohkivaara, Äkäslompolo (near Levi)
- **Rivers:** Ounas River system (north of Levi)
- **Guides available:** Contact info@leville.net for guide booking

**Equipment:**
- Rod & reel rental: €20–50 per day (available Levi center)
- Waders (chest-height): Needed for river fishing
- Tackle box: Lures, hooks, line (or rent)

**Best Time of Day:**
- Early morning (5–7 AM): Most active
- Evening (7–10 PM): Second best (midnight sun = longer fishing hours)
- Midday: Slower (heat, light intensity)

**Accommodation Advantage:**
- Leville.net properties allow self-catering prep of catch
- Some properties have freezer space for storing fish
- Quiet locations good for fishing contemplation

---

### D3. Mountain Biking

**Levi Terrain Park Conversion:**
- Winter terrain park (jumps, rails) converted to summer bike trails
- Lift-served mountain biking (chairlift access to trails)
- Downhill-focused trails

**Terrain:**
- **Beginner:** Smooth paths, minimal elevation change, scenic loops
- **Intermediate:** Technical sections, roots, rocks, moderate climbs
- **Advanced:** Steep descents, jumps, drops, challenging terrain

**Season:** June–August (snow-free, best conditions)

**Bike Rental:**
- Available in Levi center
- Types: Hardtail (lighter, more efficient), full suspension (comfort, control)
- Cost: €30–60 per day
- Helmets mandatory (provided)

**Difficulty:**
- Beginner-friendly trails exist (not all advanced)
- Chairlift access means easier climbing, more riding time
- Multiple trails allow progression from easy to hard

**Duration:**
- Short rides: 1–2 hours
- Full day: 4–6 hours (multiple trails, rest breaks)

**Events:**
- Mountain bike festivals (varies by year, check locally)
- Races & competitions (summer season)

---

### D4. Photography & Nature

**Landscape Photography:**
- **Midnight sun:** May 24–July 20 (golden light 24 hours during peak)
- **Best locations:** Levi fell summit, lake reflections, forest scenes
- **Peak season:** June–July

**Wildlife Photography:**
- **Subjects:** Reindeer, birds (eagles, ptarmigan), occasional larger animals
- **Best time:** Early morning (wildlife most active)
- **Equipment:** Telephoto lens (200mm+ preferred), patience

**Wildflower Photography:**
- **Peak:** Mid-late July
- **Macro equipment:** Helpful for flower detail shots
- **Weather:** Variable (overcast better for flower detail, sun creates glare)

**Guides Available:**
- Landscape photography workshops (local photographers)
- Wildlife photography tours (experienced guides)
- Customizable private tours

## E. YEAR-ROUND EXPERIENCES

### E1. Finnish Sauna Culture (Sauna Opas)

**What is Sauna?**
- Traditional Finnish bathing ritual, dating back 2,000+ years
- Health and wellness practice (not sexual or inappropriate — misconception common elsewhere)
- Common in Finnish home life (95% of homes have sauna)
- Public and private versions available

**Temperature & Duration:**
- **Temperature:** 70–90°C typical (can reach 100°C+)
- **Session:** 10–20 minutes (beginners), 20–30 minutes (experienced)
- **Frequency:** 1–3 times per week typical for Finns
- **Hydration:** Critical (drink water before/after)

**Sauna Types:**
- **Electric sauna:** Most common (modern, convenient, controlled temperature)
- **Smoke sauna (savusauna):** Traditional (wood-fired, slower heating, intense experience)
- **Public saunas:** Rare but exist in some towns (separate male/female hours)
- **Private:** Most Leville.net properties have private saunas (no etiquette concerns)

**Procedure (Private Sauna):**
1. Shower with soap (cleanse body)
2. Enter sauna in underwear or naked (your choice in private)
3. Sit 10–20 minutes (can pour water on rocks = "löyly" = steam burst)
4. Exit to cool down (step outside, splash cold water, or jump in snow/lake)
5. Repeat 2–3 times
6. Final rinse with cool shower
7. Rest & cool completely

**Cooling Options:**
- **Outside:** Roll in snow (winter), jump in lake (summer)
- **Shower:** Cool/cold water
- **Air cooling:** Simply step outside (northern climates provide natural cooling)

**Health Benefits (Claimed):**
- Relaxation, stress relief
- Improved circulation
- Muscle recovery (post-exercise)
- Skin health
- Mental wellness

**Safety Considerations:**
- Stay hydrated (drink water, electrolytes)
- Don't use alcohol immediately before/after
- Cardiovascular conditions: Consult doctor first
- Pregnancy: Avoid high temperatures (miscarriage risk)
- Children: Can use saunas with supervision (lower temperatures)

**Etiquette (Private Sauna — No Concerns):**
- Your sauna, your rules
- Clothing optional in private settings
- Public saunas: Separate hours for genders, towel sitting only, no swimwear

**Leville.net Properties:**
- **All properties:** Private saunas (no etiquette concerns)
- **Type:** Mix of electric (modern) and traditional (Karhupirtti)
- **Temperature control:** Set your own
- **Privacy:** Complete (not shared with other guests)

---

### E2. Dining & Culinary Experience

**K-Market (Postintie, Levi Center)**
- Grocery store (convenience store category)
- Opens: 7 AM daily
- Stock: Basic groceries, fresh bread, local products
- **Pantti system:** Bottle deposit (€0.10–0.50 per bottle) refundable
- **Alko nearby:** State alcohol monopoly (beer, wine, spirits only — separate store)

**Self-Catering:**
- All Leville.net properties have full kitchens (stove, oven, dishwasher)
- K-Market provides fresh ingredients for cooking
- Fish from local catch can be prepared in vacation rental kitchens

**Restaurant Booking:**
- Multiple restaurants in Levi center
- Leville.net can arrange bookings/recommendations
- Cuisines: Finnish, international, seasonal menus

**Dining Culture Notes:**
- Early dinner hour (typical Finns eat 5–6 PM)
- Lunch (lounaspaketti) often best-value meals (set menu, ~€12–15)
- Coffee culture strong (multiple café breaks daily)

**Seasonal Specialties:**
- **Winter:** Reindeer meat (poronkäristys = traditional dish), fish
- **Summer:** Fresh berries (cloudberry, blueberry), salmon
- **Year-round:** Rye bread, dark bread, Karelian pasties

---

## F. SEASONAL INFORMATION & PLANNING

### F1. Winter (November–April)

**Climate:**
- **Temperature range:** -10 to -25°C typical
- **Coldest month:** January–February (can reach -30°C or lower)
- **Daylight:** Decreases from November to polar night (December 21 = ~4 hours daylight)
- **Polar night:** December 21–January 20 (no direct sunlight, continuous twilight)
- **Recovery:** February onward, daylight increases

**Snow Conditions:**
- **Base depth:** 50 cm (November) → 150 cm (February) → 80 cm (April)
- **Snowfall:** Regular, reliable throughout winter
- **Artificial snowmaking:** Levi uses 100% snowmaking to ensure consistent conditions

**Real-Time Data:**
- Snow report: [https://leville.net/levi/saatieto-levilta](https://leville.net/levi/saatieto-levilta)
- Updated daily with official measurements
- Includes temperature, precipitation, wind

**What to Pack:**
- **Outer layer:** Winter coat (rated -20°C+), waterproof
- **Mid-layer:** Thermal fleece or wool
- **Base layer:** Thermal underwear (merino wool preferred)
- **Feet:** Insulated boots (-20°C rating), wool socks (2 pairs)
- **Head/Hands:** Warm hat (covers ears), gloves, scarf
- **Face:** Balaclava or face mask (for -20°C+ days)
- **Eyes:** Sunglasses (snow reflects UV, eye strain)
- **Hand warmers:** Chemical packs helpful
- **Moisture-wicking:** Avoid cotton (retains sweat)

**Activities Peak:**
- Skiing, snowmobile, husky, reindeer, snowshoeing, sauna
- Aurora viewing (peak Dec–Feb)

**Darkness Challenges:**
- Polar night: Emotionally challenging for some (lack of sunlight)
- Mitigation: Get outside during twilight, use light therapy, stay active

**Health Considerations:**
- Vitamin D supplementation recommended
- Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD): Risk higher; seek sunlight, activity
- Hydration: Winter dehydration common (dry air, overheating indoors)

---

### F2. Spring (March–April)

**Climate:**
- **Temperature:** -10 to +5°C
- **Daylight:** Rapidly increasing (March 21 = 12 hours, April 1 = 16+ hours)
- **Snow melt:** Begins late March, accelerates April
- **Weather volatility:** Can shift from -10 to +5°C day-to-day

**Season Character:**
- **Early spring (March):** Still winter-like, skiing viable, aurora faint
- **Late spring (April):** Rapid melt, muddy conditions, skiing ends mid-April

**Levi Skiing Closure:**
- Typically closes **April 14** (varies by snow conditions)
- By mid-April, base deteriorates, daytime melting accelerates

**Aurora Viewing:**
- Early March: Still good (65% probability, decreasing)
- Late March: Declining (longer days = less darkness)
- April: Impossible (midnight sun = no darkness)

**Best Activities:**
- Final skiing (March peak, April declining)
- Aurora viewing (early March)
- Spring hiking (snowshoes helpful for wet snow)
- Reindeer sledding (still good snow)

**What to Pack:**
- Dual-layer clothing (warm base, easily removable mid-layer)
- Waterproof jacket (wet snow season)
- Gaiters (wet snow gets into boots)
- Sunscreen (spring sun + white snow = high UV)
- Sunglasses essential

---

### F3. Summer (June–August)

**Climate:**
- **Temperature:** +15 to +20°C typical (highs +25°C possible, rare)
- **Midnight sun:** May 24–July 20 (24-hour daylight in peak)
- **Daylight hours:** 18–24 hours (incredible for activities)
- **Weather:** Variable (rain possible any day)

**Midnight Sun Experience:**
- Unique Arctic phenomenon (worth experiencing)
- Circular horizon light (not complete darkness even at "night")
- Excellent for photography (golden light 24 hours)
- May affect sleep (use blackout curtains in rentals)

**Temperature Management:**
- Can feel cooler due to northern latitude & wind
- Layering still important (not warm like southern Europe)
- Sun strong (UV index high despite moderate temperature)

**Best Activities:**
- Hiking (trails fully snow-free, wildflower peak July)
- Fishing (water accessible, fish feeding summer)
- Biking (terrain park & trails)
- Photography (light quality exceptional)
- Midnight sun tours (educational)

**What to Pack:**
- Light layers (fleece, not winter coat)
- Rain jacket (variable weather)
- Hiking boots (muddy/wet terrain)
- Sun protection (hat, sunscreen SPF 30+)
- Insect repellent (mosquitoes July–August)
- Long sleeves/pants (insect + sun protection)

**Bugs:**
- **Mosquitoes:** Most abundant July–August, worst in wet areas
- **Midges:** Small, bothersome, peak twilight hours
- **Mitigation:** DEET repellent, head nets, long clothing

---

### F4. Autumn/Ruska (September–October)

**Climate:**
- **Temperature:** +5 to +10°C early Sep, dropping to -5°C by late Oct
- **Daylight:** Decreasing rapidly (12 hours Sep 21, 8 hours Oct 21)
- **Precipitation:** Rain more common than winter snow

**Ruska (Fall Colors):**
- **Peak:** Mid-late September (varies by weather)
- **Colors:** Golden birch, red subarctic vegetation
- **Photography:** Excellent opportunity (saturated colors, clear light)
- **Duration:** 2–3 weeks peak color

**Aurora Return:**
- **Late September:** Faint aurora visible (requires clear skies)
- **October:** Aurora strengthens as darkness increases
- **Photography:** Increasingly viable late October

**Activities:**
- **Hiking:** Fall colors (mid-late Sep peak)
- **Photography:** Landscape & aurora combo
- **Berry picking:** Cloudberry, blueberry season
- **Fishing:** Still good (water accessible, fish pre-winter feeding)

**Weather Variability:**
- Rain frequent (intermittent, not continuous)
- Snow possible late October (usually doesn't stick until November)
- Wind can be strong (plan accordingly)

**What to Pack:**
- Warm fall layers (fleece, light insulation)
- Rain jacket (essential)
- Waterproof hiking boots
- Hat & gloves (especially Oct)
- Sun protection (still strong despite lower angle)

---

## H. ACCESSIBILITY & SPECIAL NEEDS

### H1. Wheelchair Accessibility

**Accessible Properties:**
- **Skistar 209** — 1BR, accessible bathroom, no stairs internal (entry has 1 step, small ramp possible)
- **Skistar 210** — 1BR, accessible bathroom, similar to 209
- **Levi Glacier A1** — 4BR, accessible bathroom, wheelchair accessible path
- **Levi Glacier A3** — 4BR, accessible bathroom

**Accessibility Features:**
- Grab bars in bathrooms
- Wide doorways (32"+ clearance)
- Roll-in showers (some properties)
- Accessible parking (Skistar parking area)
- Level access or minimal steps

**Limitations:**
- Skistar building has external stairs to entrance (1–2 steps, ramp possible with advance notice)
- Some areas have gravel/unpaved surfaces (snow/ice in winter)
- Mountain terrain: Limited wheelchair access for hiking

**Parking:**
- Reserved accessible parking available (Skistar)
- Free general parking (Front Slope, Glacier)

**Advance Planning:**
- Contact info@leville.net at booking to discuss specific needs
- Mobility aids: Wheelchairs, walkers provided/accommodated
- Accessible transportation: Arrange with local operators (contact Leville.net)

---

### H2. Dietary Restrictions

**Self-Catering Advantage:**
- All properties have full kitchens
- K-Market & local shops have basic & specialty foods
- Gluten-free products available (growing availability)

**Restaurant Reservations:**
- Leville.net can pre-notify restaurants of dietary needs
- Finnish cuisine: Meat/fish-based (good for carnivore/keto diets)
- Vegetarian: Less common in traditional Finnish cuisine, restaurants accommodate

**Allergies:**
- If severe (anaphylaxis), carry medications (EpiPen)
- Inform Leville.net & local providers of severe allergies
- K-Market labels products (allergen information available)

---

### H3. Medical Access

**Nearest Hospital:**
- **Rovaniemi Central Hospital:** 100 km away (~1.5 hour drive)
- **Kittilä Health Center:** 15 km away (minor injuries, consultations)

**Emergency Services:**
- **Ambulance:** Dial 112 (works from any phone)
- **Response time:** 30–45 minutes typical in Levi area
- **Air ambulance:** Available for critical emergencies

**Medications:**
- **Pharmacy:** In Levi center
- **Prescriptions:** Fill before arrival (limited availability for specific medications)
- **Over-the-counter:** Painkillers, cold meds, basic first aid available

**Insurance:**
- **EU citizens:** European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) covers emergency care
- **Non-EU:** Travel insurance strongly recommended (high costs for foreign nationals)

### I2. Policies & House Rules

**Smoking:**
- **Prohibited** indoors (outside permitted)
- Violation: €200–500 fee + property deep cleaning
- Electronic cigarettes: Generally allowed

**Noise Curfew:**
- **Quiet hours:** 10 PM–8 AM
- Respectful behavior expected
- Excessive noise: Tenant may be asked to leave (no refund)

**Guests Limits:**
- Maximum occupancy strictly enforced
- Exceeding limit: Eviction possible
- Confirm group size at booking

**Pets:**
- **Allowed in:** Front Slope, Glacier, Bear Lodge, others (verify booking)
- **Not allowed in:** Skistar (generally)
- **Fees:** €30/pet typical
- **Restrictions:** Pets must not disturb neighbors, damage property

**Check-in/Check-out:**
- **Check-in:** 4 PM (earlier possible if property ready, contact first)
- **Check-out:** 10 AM (late checkout €20–50/hour, subject to next booking)
- **Keys:** Electronic entry (code provided at check-in)

**Parking:**
- **Included:** Most properties (free)
- **Reserved:** Some lots, confirm at booking
- **Winter:** Clear snow from vehicle (safety requirement)

---

### I3. Cleaning & Maintenance

**Final Cleaning:**
- **Optional add-on:** Final cleaning is bookable as an add-on; check property-specific terms in the booking confirmation
- **Property condition:** Return in "normal use" condition
- **Damage:** Tenant responsible for damage beyond normal wear

**Linen:**
- **Optional add-on:** Bed linens (sheets, pillowcases) and towels are an add-on service – book during reservation or bring your own. Not included in the nightly price by default.
- **Extra guest fee:** €19/person (when linens are booked)
- **Laundry:** €2 per wash (basement facility, card payment)

**Trash/Recycling:**
- Recycling bins in properties (sort glass, paper, plastic, organic)
- Trash: Place in designated bins outside

**Maintenance Issues:**
- **Report during stay:** Contact immediately (24-hour response)
- **After checkout:** Document photos, email info@leville.net

## K. LEVI REGION CONTEXT

### K1. About Levi Ski Resort

**Location:** Levi fell, Kittilä municipality, Finnish Lapland

**History:**
- First ski lift: 1960s
- Modern expansion: 1980s–1990s
- Current size: ~15 slopes, 7 lifts

**Market Position:**
- Third-largest ski resort in Finland (after Ruka, Ylläs by terrain)
- Closest to Kittilä Airport (15 km)
- Most accessible from southern Finland (nearest to major population centers)
- Competitor: Ylläs (30 km), Ruka (60 km), Saariselkä (200+ km)

**Summer Use:**
- Terrain park converted to bike trails
- No skiing, but activities available (hiking, fishing, biking)

### K2. Kittilä Town

**Distance:** 15 km from Levi
- Airport (KTT): 15 km
- Grocery, fuel, restaurants: In town
- Healthcare: Kittilä Health Center + Regional Hospital

**Region:** Kolari–Kittilä axis = main travel corridor
